nodes.name: NF-PBA Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: 0.6 mmol of nickel nitrate and 0.9 mmol of sodium citrate were first dissolved in 20 mL of Milli-Q water. Next, 0.4 mmol of potassium hexacyanoferrate (III) was dissolved in another 20 mL of Milli-Q water. The two solutions were then mixed and vigorous stirring was conducted for 12 h to synthesize the NF-PBA precursor with uniformly distributed particle sizes. It is well known that the citrate ions prohibit the precipitation reaction from forming large-sized particles. Therefore, a sufficient reaction time was required to prepare uniformly distributed precursors with small sized particles.

nodes.name: NC-PBA Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: The NC-PBA precursor was synthesized by the same method as NF-PBA, except for the use of 0.4 mmol potassium hexacyanocobaltate (III) solution instead of potassium hexacyanoferrate (III). 0.6 mmol of nickel nitrate and 0.9 mmol of sodium citrate were first dissolved in 20 mL of Milli-Q water. Next, 0.4 mmol of potassium hexacyanocobaltate (III) was dissolved in another 20 mL of Milli-Q water. The two solutions were then mixed and vigorous stirring was conducted for 12 h.

nodes.name: NCF-PBA Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: The NCF-PBA precursor was synthesized by the same method as NF-PBA, except using a mixed solution of 0.2 mmol potassium hexacyanocobaltate (III) and 0.2 mmol potassium hexacyanoferrate (III). 0.6 mmol of nickel nitrate and 0.9 mmol of sodium citrate were first dissolved in 20 mL of Milli-Q water. Next, a mixed solution of 0.2 mmol potassium hexacyanocobaltate (III) and 0.2 mmol potassium hexacyanoferrate (III) was dissolved in another 20 mL of Milli-Q water. The two solutions were then mixed and vigorous stirring was conducted for 12 h.

nodes.name: MOF Hydrothermal Transformation
nodes.procedure: 100 mg of PBA precursor (NF-PBA, NC-PBA, or NCF-PBA) and 200 mg of Na2S were mixed in 100 mL of ethanol and transferred into a Teflon liner and stainless-steel autoclave. The hydrothermal reaction was carried out at 100°C for 6 h to induce sufficient ion exchange. Then, the intermediate product was washed, dried, ground, and heat treated at 300°C in Ar atmosphere for 3 h to form highly crystalline MOFs. The black recrystallized MOFs were pulverized and dried in a vacuum oven at 70°C for 12 h. The final MOF products containing Ni/Co, Ni/Fe, and Ni/Co/Fe centers were denoted NC-MOF, NF-MOF, and NCF-MOF, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NC-MOF shows nanocuboidal structures with average size 400 nm and large face-centered pores. NF-MOF shows uniformly sized cuboidal structures average size 160 nm maintaining precursor morphology. NCF-MOF exhibits cuboid morphology average size 180 nm with roughened surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For example, NC-MOF ... showed nanocuboidal structures with an average size of 400 nm and relatively large pores on each face (Figure 1A,B), while NF-MOF ... showed uniformly sized cuboidal structures with an average size of 160 nm, maintaining the initial PBA precursor morphology (Figure 1D,E). NCF-MOF ... exhibited general cuboid morphology with an average size of 180 nm and roughened surfaces (Figure 1G,H).

properties.features: Rough, porous-like surface with hollow or bubble-like structures

nodes.characterization_summary: NC-MOF shows interconnected large pores forming hollow core. NF-MOF maintains nonporous nanocuboidal structure consistent with SEM. NCF-MOF shows spots of different brightness within single nanocuboid indicating multiple internal voids.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis was conducted to reveal the internal morphological features of the MOF catalysts. NC-MOF under TEM revealed that the large pores observed on all faces of the nanocuboids were in fact interconnected, resulting in a hollow core (Figure 1C). NF-MOF, on the other hand, maintained the nonporous nanocuboidal structure from its precursor (Figure 1F), consistent with the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) observations. TEM observations of NCF-MOF revealed spots within a single nanocuboid with different brightness (Figure 1I), indicative of multiple void formations.

nodes.characterization_summary: NC-MOF EDS line-scans show higher element intensities at ends vs center confirming hollow core porous structure. NF-MOF shows larger Ni/Fe amounts, lower uniform C/S/N distribution. NCF-MOF shows uniform Ni/Co/Fe distribution along middle/edge indicating partial ion exchange creating multiple voids.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning TEM (STEM) of a single NC-MOF nanocuboid was used to obtain energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) line-scans ... The plots clearly show that the intensities of all detected elements are relatively higher at both ends of the plot compared to the center, which confirms the internally connected porous structure with a hollow core ... relatively larger amounts of nickel and iron were detected within NF-MOF with lower amounts of carbon, sulfur, and nitrogen uniformly distributed ... the results obtained from EDS line-scans ... of NCF-MOF show that the three transition metals (nickel, cobalt, and iron) are uniformly distributed along the middle and the edge of nanocuboids.

nodes.characterization_summary: NC-MOF SAED patterns reveal FCC lattice structures at center and edge. NF-MOF SAED indicates polycrystalline FCC structure at center/edge. NCF-MOF SAED shows [001] orientation at face center and [111] at edge corresponding to FCC structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images obtained from NC-MOF ... selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns were also obtained at the center and the edge of the nanocuboids, both of which reveal FCC lattice structures. ... SAED patterns obtained at the center (Figure S4C, Supporting Information) and the edge (Figure S4D, Supporting Information) of the nanocuboid indicate a polycrystalline FCC structure. ... The crystal structure of NCF-MOF confirmed by SAED patterns obtained from HRTEM images at the face center (Figure 2C) and the edge (Figure 2D) reveal [001] and [111] orientations, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NC-MOF elemental maps confirm composition of Ni, N, S, C, residual Co showing near-complete Co(CN)₆³⁻ to S²⁻ exchange forming hollow NiS. NF-MOF shows larger Ni/Fe. NCF-MOF shows uniform Ni/Co/Fe/S/C/N distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: dark-field TEM (DFTEM) and elemental mapping were conducted to verify the compositional characteristics of NC-MOF ... The elemental maps indicate that NC-MOF is composed of nickel, nitrogen, sulfur, carbon, and residual cobalt ... DFTEM elemental mapping (Figure S4E-J, Supporting Information) results, relatively larger amounts of nickel and iron were detected within NF-MOF ... DFTEM elemental mapping (Figure 2E-K) of NCF-MOF show that the three transition metals ... are uniformly distributed.

nodes.characterization_summary: NF-MOF has BET surface area of 27.4 m²/g and pore volume of 0.14 cc/g. NCF-MOF has BET surface area of 50.7 m²/g and pore volume of 0.29 cc/g, both showing hysteresis loops indicating mesopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NCF-MOF adsorbed a much greater volume of N₂ resulting in a 50.7 m² g⁻¹ Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, compared to only 27.4 m² g⁻¹ obtained with NF-MOF. In terms of the pore size distribution ... NCF-MOF was found to have two times the accumulative pore volume compared to NF-MOF (0.29 vs 0.14 ccg⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: NC-MOF shows Ni 2p and S 2p peaks corresponding to NiS and Ni₃S₂. NF-MOF mainly Ni²⁺, Fe with 27% 3+ and 73% 2+. NCF-MOF shows Ni²⁺ (5.4% NiS), Fe 43% 2+ 57% 3+, Co 17% 2+ 83% 3+, low intensity S peak. N 1s: NF-MOF 98.7% C≡N, NCF-MOF 94.7% C≡N + 4.24% pyridinic N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni 2p ... and S 2p ... spectra of NC-MOF show peaks found at binding energies that correspond to NiS and Ni₃S₂ ... NCF-MOF, on the other hand, was found to be composed of Ni in 2+ states (Figure 3A), Fe in 43% and 57% of 2+ and 3+ states (Figure 3B), and Co in 17% and 83% of 2+ and 3+ states (Figure 3C) ... N species found in NF-MOF predominantly existed as C≡N (98.7%) ... NCF-MOF ... also contained pyridinic N species (4.24%) (Figure 3F).
